mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to exist where a clinical-role user has outcome=Permitted for Read or AddNote without active care-team membership. This directly violates the core access-control invariant that clinical record access requires documented care-team membership.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_CareTeamBypass { some u: User, p: Patient, ae: AuditEntry | u.role in (Doctor + Nurse + Pharmacist + ClinicalAdmin) and ae.user = u and ae.patient = p and ae.access_type in (Read + AddNote) and ae.outcome = Permitted and (no ctm: CareTeamMembership | ctm.clinician = u and ctm.patient = p and ctm.status = ActiveMembership) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows two distinct ClinicalNote instances with the same id to have different authors or content, violating the append-only guarantee that is essential to clinical record immutability and legal defensibility.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MutableNote { some disj n1, n2: ClinicalNote | n1.id = n2.id and n1.author != n2.author }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows two distinct AuditEntry instances (same user, timestamp) to have different outcomes or access_types, violating the immutability guarantee that is essential for audit integrity and compliance with healthcare regulations.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_MutableAuditEntry { some disj ae1, ae2: AuditEntry | ae1.user = ae2.user and ae1.patient = ae2.patient and ae1.outcome != ae2.outcome }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to record an incorrect user_role snapshot (e.g., recording a doctor as HospitalAdministrator). This breaks the trustworthiness of audit attribution and enables forensic manipulation or misattribution of access events.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditMisattribution { some u: User, ae: AuditEntry | ae.user = u and ae.user_role != u.role }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows HospitalAdministrator users to perform Read or AddNote operations, violating the principle that administrators can only audit the log and must never view clinical content, which is a critical privacy and access-control boundary.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AdminAccessViolation { some u: User, ae: AuditEntry | u.role = HospitalAdministrator and ae.user = u and ae.access_type in (Read + AddNote) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Removing this fact allows audit entries to record a note_id in contexts where it should not be present (e.g., for a denied AddNote or a Read operation), or to omit it when it should be present. This can enable unintended clinical-content leakage or audit-structural inconsistency.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_NoteIdInconsistency { some ae: AuditEntry | ((ae.access_type = AddNote and ae.outcome = Permitted and no ae.note_id) or (ae.access_type = Read and some ae.note_id)) }
